title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from p.5: G is an affine Q-group (a quotient of the motivic Galois group). It carries a weight cocharacter i: G_m -> G (central) and a character ε: G -> G_m (the 'Tate/degree' character). G' = Ker ε, η = i(-1), and G ≅ G' ×_{Z/2} G_m. A Hodge datum is a homomorphism h: S -> G_R, where S = Res_{C/R} G_m is the Deligne torus. h is subject to (a) the total degree is the one given by i, and (b) Q(-1) has bidegree (1,1). Equivalently it is h': U(1) -> G'_R with h'(-1) = η. The theorem of p.5 says the following are equivalent: every V in Rep(G) of degree n admits a G-invariant polarization φ: V⊗V -> Q(-n); the same over R; and, implied by these, the centralizer of h(C) (C = h(i)) is maximal compact. Modulo the centre, this is the condition 'h(i) is a Cartan involution'.

This page, step by step:
1. Definition. Let S be a complex analytic space. A rigidified G-subordination on S is a ⊗-functor V ↦ (Hodge family on the trivial bundle V_S = V_C × S). Concretely this is:
   - a real-analytic bigrading V_S = ⊕ V_S^{p,q} with V_S^{q,p} equal to the conjugate of V_S^{p,q};
   - whose Hodge filtration F^p is a holomorphic subbundle filtration;
   - with marginal normalisations: total degree given by i, and Q(-1) of type (1,1);
   - such that each fibre is polarisable by a G-invariant form φ: V⊗V -> Q(-n) for V homogeneous of degree n.
2. Margin remark. If S is connected it suffices to require this at one point s0. The fixed G-invariant φ is automatically a morphism of Hodge structures everywhere, and positivity propagates (it is open, and closed by non-degeneracy).
3. Pointwise analysis, ignoring holomorphy. Tannakian reconstruction gives, for each s, a homomorphism j(s): S -> G_R, equivalently j'(s): U -> G'_R with j'(s)(-1) = η. The polarisability theorem makes Zent_{G'_R}(j'(s)(C)) maximal compact. The map s ↦ j(s) is real-analytic.
4. Next page. The set D of such j is given a natural complex structure. Holomorphy of the filtration becomes holomorphy of S -> D. So the functor S ↦ {rigidified G-subordinations on S} is represented by D, with G(R) acting and components of the form G(R)^0/H(R)∩G(R)^0.
5. A crossed-out continuation passes to a lattice V_0, its stabiliser Γ ⊂ G(Q), and hence to quotients Γ\D.

Purpose: a Tannakian, group-theoretic construction of the classifying space of (polarisable) Hodge structures with 'motivic' symmetry group G. It is a period domain / Mumford–Tate domain viewed as a fine moduli space, written within the 1965 motivic Galois group programme, with the arithmetic quotients that become Shimura-type varieties in view.
errors: No Griffiths transversality condition is imposed. Only holomorphy of the Hodge filtration is required, so the objects are holomorphic families of Hodge structures, not VHS; geometric families (and Shimura data, via Deligne's condition that h only involves types (-1,1),(0,0),(1,-1) on Lie G) satisfy more. Thus D represents a larger functor than the one relevant for motives in families, except when D is Hermitian symmetric.

The condition 'Zent_{G'_R}(j'(C)) compact maximal' is only correct modulo the centre (or after dividing by i(R^{*+}), as Grothendieck himself corrected on p.5). If the centre of G'_R has non-compact part, the centraliser cannot be compact.
Sign inconsistency: the crossed-out text has φ: V⊗V -> Q(n), whereas p.5 and the normalisation 'Q(-1) of type (1,1)' require Q(-n).
The margin argument for connected S needs positivity to be both open and closed. Closedness uses non-degeneracy of φ restricted to the Hodge pieces; this is only sketched.

ideas.what: Hodge structures as representations of the Deligne torus S, with weight/Tate normalisation via i and ε, and a tensor-functor (Tannakian) definition of a family of Hodge structures with symmetry group G
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structures as S-representations; G-valued (Tannakian) variations of Hodge structure / Hodge data (G,h)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971; Travaux de Shimura, 1971); Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972, with Grothendieck's ideas acknowledged); Simpson for G-VHS
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. Transmitted via Saavedra's thesis and Grothendieck's correspondence; Grothendieck mentions motivic Galois group ideas in Récoltes et Semailles without such details.

ideas.what: Polarisability of all tensor constructions via a G-invariant polarisation equivalent to a maximal-compact (Cartan involution) condition on the centraliser of h(i), pointwise in families
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's criterion: ad h(i) is a Cartan involution of G^ad_R (polarisable Hodge structures with Mumford–Tate group G)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979); Satake; Mumford for Hodge groups

ideas.what: The set D of admissible h carries a complex structure; rigidified families on S correspond to holomorphic maps S -> D, i.e. D represents the functor; components are G(R)^0/H(R)
ideas.modern_name: Period domain / Mumford–Tate domain as fine moduli space of marked (rigidified) Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (Periods of integrals I–III, 1968–70); Deligne 1979; Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012)

ideas.what: For connected S, the polarisation condition only needs checking at one point when the form is G-invariant
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of polarisations in families (open-closed argument)

missed.claim: Already in 1965, Grothendieck works with the Deligne torus S, the U(1) reformulation h'(-1) = η, a Tannakian definition of families of Hodge structures with symmetry group G, and their classifying domain D as a representing object. This predates Mumford 1966 (Hodge groups), Griffiths 1968 (period domains) and Deligne 1971 (Hodge II / Travaux de Shimura) for the S-formalism. The usual attribution of 'Hodge structure = representation of S' and 'Mumford–Tate domain as moduli' to Deligne, Griffiths and Green–Griffiths–Kerr misses this documented 1965 anticipation within the motivic Galois group programme.
missed.quote: Une G-subordination rigidifiée sur S est la donnée d'une ⊗-fonction qui, à tout V ∈ Ob Rep(G), associe une structure de famille de Hodge ... donnée par une j = j(s) : S → G_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is history-of-ideas evidence that the Tannakian/Shimura-datum viewpoint on Hodge theory originated in Grothendieck's motivic Galois group programme. It is relevant to credit discussions around Deligne and Saavedra.

missed.claim: The crossed-out continuation on p.7 (a lattice V_0, its stabiliser Γ ⊂ G(Q), and the induced family on Γ\D) begins a moduli interpretation of arithmetic quotients of the domains of 'motivic' Hodge data. This is essentially Shimura varieties as moduli of motives with G-structure. It was abandoned, and transversality was never added.
missed.quote: Donc pour S variable, on a un foncteur représentable par D
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates Deligne's 1979 motivic interpretation of Shimura varieties and the later 'moduli of motives' viewpoint. However, the idea is now well established, so there is little new mathematical content.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically nothing beyond what Deligne, Griffiths and Green–Griffiths–Kerr later established (and the version here lacks transversality). Historically, though, the explicit 1965 use of the Deligne torus, the Cartan-involution polarisation criterion, and the representability of the Hodge-datum domain by Grothendieck is a notable unpublished priority detail.
transcription_corrections: 'on vient une façon de' is more likely 'on veut une façon de' (or 'on a').
'puisqu'elle est un dég. fermé[?]' plausibly reads 'puisqu'elle est non dég. partout' (non-degenerate everywhere). That is the argument needed for positivity to be closed.
The insertion over 'famille de Hodge' read as 'graduée[?] isogène[?]' is probably 'polarisable (mod isogénie)'-type wording; '(mod isogénie)' is clearly repeated in a) below.
In the margin, 'SF[?] dans bidegré (1,1)' should be read as 'Q(-1) donne SH dans bidegré (1,1)', i.e. the Hodge structure of Q(-1) is pure of type (1,1).
'Zent_{G'_R}(j'(s)(C))': here C is the element h(i) from p.5, not the complex numbers.
